document.title: [Excised] Believe Pakistan is Backing Taliban
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Secret] Conveys a source's belief that Pakistan directly supports the Taliban, with General Babar as principal patron. Pakistani Frontier Corps allegedly provided artillery cover for the Taliban's seizure of the Spin Boldak arms dump.

mentions.quote: MEETING WITH ISI DIRGEN LTGEN. GENERAL ASHRAF THE PREVIOUS WEEK
HAD VEHEMENTLY DENIED THAT HIS AGENCY HAD ANY ROLE IN SUPPORTING THE AFGHAN TALIBAN MOVEMENT
THE GENERAL PREDICTED THAT THE TALIBAN COULD BECOME A DANGEROUS AND UNCONTROLLABLE FORCE
HE HAD STRONGLY RECOMMENDED TO PM BHUTTO THAT THE GOP NOT SUPPORT THE TALIBAN IN ANY WAY

events.description: Taliban seize Spin Boldak armory after shelling from Pakistani Frontier Corps positions, per source.
Meeting with ISI DG Ashraf in which he denied ISI support for Taliban (week before Nov 9).
Source confides to Embassy political officer about the Ashraf meeting.
Embassy cable sent to State Department.
Taliban seize Spin Boldak armory after artillery shelling allegedly from Pakistani Frontier Corps positions.
Taliban rout NIFA commander Lallai and HIG commander Sar Katib in Kandahar using tanks and helicopters.
Source accompanied to Kabul a meeting with ISI DG Ashraf, who denied ISI support to Taliban; source told Poloff on November 9.
U.S. Embassy Islamabad cables that a source believes Pakistan is backing the Taliban.

sources_cited: Excised well-informed source's account to Embassy poloff, 9 Nov 1994
key_claims: A source claims the Taliban are directly supported by Pakistan.
ISI DG Ashraf reportedly denied ISI support and warned Bhutto that the Taliban could become dangerous and uncontrollable.
The source alleges Frontier Corps shelling and Pakistani officers' coordination enabled the Sept 1994 capture of Spin Boldak armory.
Taliban defeat of NIFA and HIG commanders using tanks and helicopters suggested Pakistani tutelage.
The Embassy doubts the source accurately characterized Ashraf but accepts some Pakistani elements supported the Taliban, with continued support and government control uncertain.
